name: Faivelo API
description:
The Faivelo API lets you manage domains, mailboxes and aliases, and send, read,
search and organise mail — everything the dashboard and webmail can do.

## Authentication

Send your API key as a Bearer token:

```
Authorization: Bearer fvl_live_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
```

Create and manage keys in **Settings → Developers**
(https://faivelo.com/settings/developers). The full key is shown only once at
creation. The API is included on every paid plan and during the free trial;
requests from an account without one are refused with `402 plan_required`.

## Scopes

Each key carries a set of scopes; a request fails with **403** if the key lacks
the scope it needs:

| Scope | Grants |
| --- | --- |
| `domains:read` | List and read domains |
| `mailboxes:read` | List and read mailboxes |
| `mailboxes:write` | Create, update, delete mailboxes, reset passwords |
| `aliases:read` | List aliases |
| `aliases:write` | Create and delete aliases |
| `dns:read` | List a domain's live DNS records |
| `dns:write` | Create, update and delete DNS records |
| `mail:read` | List, read and search messages; list folders; download attachments |
| `mail:send` | Send mail |
| `mail:write` | Flag, move, delete and mark messages as spam |
| `drive:read` | List files and folders in the account's Faivelo Drive and get file download URLs |

A key may optionally be **restricted to a single mailbox**, in which case it may
only hold `mail:*` scopes and can only act on that mailbox.

## Agent keys (AI agents)

Keys come in two kinds: `account` (the default — full account access within
its scopes) and `agent`. An **agent key** is a credential for an AI agent: it
may create mailboxes, but it can only operate mailboxes **it created or was
explicitly granted** — it can never read other mailboxes, add or remove domains
or aliases, touch billing, or create more API keys. Agent keys may only hold the
`mailboxes:read`, `mailboxes:write`, `dns:read`, `dns:write` and
`mail:*` scopes; DNS edits to mail-critical records (MX/SPF/DKIM/…) require
an explicit `force` flag.

Create one with `kind: "agent"` in **Settings → API Keys** (or via
`POST /api/user/api-keys`), hand it to your agent, and the agent can provision
its own mailbox and use it:

```bash
# 1. Agent creates its own mailbox
curl -X POST https://faivelo.com/api/v1/mailboxes \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer fvl_live_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"domain": "yourdomain.com", "localPart": "my-agent"}'

# 2. Agent sends mail from it
curl -X POST https://faivelo.com/api/v1/mailboxes/my-agent@yourdomain.com/send \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer fvl_live_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"to": "someone@example.com", "subject": "Hello", "text": "From my own mailbox."}'

# 3. Agent polls the inbox (e.g. for a verification code)
curl "https://faivelo.com/api/v1/mailboxes/my-agent@yourdomain.com/messages?folder=INBOX&limit=10" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer fvl_live_..."

# 4. Agent reads a message in full
curl "https://faivelo.com/api/v1/mailboxes/my-agent@yourdomain.com/messages/42" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer fvl_live_..."
```

## MCP server

The same four operations are exposed as MCP tools — `create_mailbox`,
`send_message`, `list_messages`, `read_message` — over Streamable HTTP at
`https://faivelo.com/api/mcp`, authenticated with the same API keys
(`Authorization: Bearer fvl_live_...`). Clients that can't set headers can
embed the key in the URL instead: `https://faivelo.com/api/mcp/fvl_live_...`.

Example configuration (Claude Code):

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http faivelo https://faivelo.com/api/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer fvl_live_..."
```

Or in a JSON MCP client config:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "faivelo": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://faivelo.com/api/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer fvl_live_..." }
    }
  }
}
```

## Responses

Successful responses use the envelope `{ "success": true, "data": ... }`.

## Errors

Every error response carries a stable machine-readable `code`, a human
`error` message, a `fix` sentence that says what to change, and a `docs`
link to that code's entry:

```json
{
  "success": false,
  "error": "This API key is missing the required scope: mail:send",
  "code": "insufficient_scope",
  "fix": "Create a key that includes the \"mail:send\" scope at https://faivelo.com/settings/developers and use it instead; scopes cannot be added to an existing key.",
  "docs": "https://faivelo.com/docs/developers/errors#insufficient_scope",
  "statusCode": 403
}
```

Validation errors (`validation_error`) also name the field at fault in
`param`. Branch on `code`, never on the message text. A `429` carries a
`Retry-After` header. Every code is listed at
https://faivelo.com/docs/developers/errors.

## Rate limits

Requests are limited to **120 per minute per key** (REST and MCP share the same
budget). A single key may create at most **10 mailboxes per rolling 24 hours**.

Sending counts against two shared pools: your plan's **monthly send limit** and
your account's **earned daily allowance**, which starts conservative and grows
automatically with clean sending history (see
[Sending limits](https://faivelo.com/docs/sending/limits/)). A rejected send
names the limit it hit, so your code can tell "wait until tomorrow" from
"monthly quota reached". Exceeding a limit returns **429** / **403**.

## Partner API

Approved partners resell Faivelo mailboxes under their own brand. A **partner
key** (kind `partner`) acts on your end customers, never on your own
account, and can only hold the two partner scopes:

| Scope | Grants |
| --- | --- |
| `partner:read` | List customers, read health, domains, mailboxes and the outbox |
| `partner:write` | Create and pause customers, add domains, set branding, create mailboxes, reset passwords |

Partner endpoints live under `/api/partner` (not `/api/v1`). A customer
that is not yours reads as **404**, never 403, so a key learns nothing about
other accounts. Partner keys are refused by `/api/v1` and the MCP server;
account and agent keys are refused by `/api/partner`.

### Sandbox mode

Mint a partner key with **Sandbox** and it starts with `fvl_test_`
instead of `fvl_live_`. Same endpoints, same responses, but every customer
it creates is a **sandbox** (`sandbox: true`): domains come back verified
the moment they are added, mailboxes exist only as rows with credentials,
nothing touches the mail server, no seat lands on your invoice, no email
goes to anyone, and nothing counts in the reputation ladder, reports or
outbox. Live and sandbox customers are disjoint: a live key never sees
sandbox customers and a test key never sees live ones. One endpoint exists
for sandbox only: `DELETE /customers/{id}` erases a sandbox customer.
Anything left is erased after 30 days.

### Plans and seats

Every end customer is on a plan you choose: `STARTER`, `GROWTH` or
`PRO`. The plan sets the customer's domain and storage limits (mailboxes
are unlimited on every plan) and the monthly seat you pay for it; prices
are on faivelo.com/partners.
Pass `plan` when you create a customer (default: your partner account's
default plan) and change it later with `POST /customers/{id}/plan`. A
downgrade is refused while the customer holds more domains than the new
plan allows. Past 20 live customers every seat is discounted
automatically.

### The onboarding loop

```bash
# 1. Create the customer (you attest the lists are first-party and that
#    you accepted the end-customer terms on their behalf)
curl -X POST https://faivelo.com/api/partner/customers \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer fvl_live_..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email":"owner@smiledental.example","companyName":"Smile Dental",
       "attestation":{"firstPartyListsOnly":true,"termsAcceptedOnBehalf":true}}'

# 2. Add their domain; the response lists the DNS records to show them
curl -X POST https://faivelo.com/api/partner/customers/CUSTOMER_ID/domains \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer fvl_live_..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"domain":"smiledental.example","brandName":"Smile Dental"}'

# 3. Poll with verify=true until verified is true
curl "https://faivelo.com/api/partner/customers/CUSTOMER_ID/domains/smiledental.example?verify=true" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer fvl_live_..."

# 4. Create a mailbox; the password and IMAP/SMTP settings come back once
curl -X POST https://faivelo.com/api/partner/customers/CUSTOMER_ID/domains/smiledental.example/mailboxes \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer fvl_live_..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"localPart":"hello","displayName":"Smile Dental"}'
```

The same loop in the SDK: `faivelo.partner.customers.create`,
`faivelo.partner.domains.add`, `faivelo.partner.domains.get(..., { verify: true })`,
`faivelo.partner.mailboxes.create`.

### Reading and sending mail from your own product

A partner key provisions accounts; it is refused by `/api/v1`. To render an
inbox, search, or send from a customer's mailboxes in your own UI, mint a
**mailbox key** on that customer with `POST /customers/{id}/api-keys`
(`faivelo.partner.apiKeys.create`). It is an ordinary account key on the
customer, limited to `mailboxes:read`, `mail:read`, `mail:send` and
`mail:write`, optionally bound to one mailbox, and shown once. Use it with
the **Mailboxes** endpoints under `/api/v1` (folders, messages, search,
send, move, flag, spam, attachments), exactly as the customer would. It stops
working while the customer is paused or suspended and when you revoke it.
Sandbox customers have no mail store, so mailbox keys need a live customer.

### Sending health and pauses

Every customer is a separate sending tenant with its own reputation. A
customer's health (`GET /customers/{id}`) reports its own 30-day bounce and
complaint rates, whether it is over the pause threshold on its own numbers,
and the tenant's sending state. You can pause a customer yourself; a lock set
by a Faivelo abuse control (`lockedBy: "faivelo"`) or a suspension is not
lifted by `resume`.

New customers send under a **trial ceiling** until they earn the standard
one on clean history (`relayCeiling`). Provisioning is refused with **403**
while your partner account is paused or at its customer cap.
